observation_summary: The DatasetUtilities.iterateRangeBounds and iterateDomainBounds methods were failing with a NullPointerException (or incorrect range calculation) because they were not correctly considering all components of the interval data (the central value, start value, and end value) when calculating the minimum and maximum bounds.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves adding logic to correctly incorporate the central 'value' (getXValue/getYValue) into the min/max calculations, and ensuring that both the minimum and maximum are updated for each component (start, end, and central value) if they are not NaN. This is a correction of the computational logic used to determine the bounds of the dataset, which is an algorithmic error in the procedure.
evidence_used: The fix_diff_oracle shows that the code was missing the inclusion of the central 'value' in the min/max calculations.

The fix_diff_oracle shows that the existing logic for 'lvalue' and 'uvalue' was incomplete, as it only updated one bound (minimum or maximum) instead of both, which is a flaw in the computational procedure.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix adds checks for Double.isNaN, the primary purpose of these checks is to facilitate the correct computation of the range, not just to guard against nulls or invalid inputs.
